hypothesis: Requiring k consecutive threshold exceedances before issuing an alarm removes short all-negative alarm episodes and raises episode and window precision without losing positive runs. Unproven; may lower recall and delay alarms.
rule: Alarm at hour t of one HARP only if windows t-k+1..t are exactly one hour apart and all have probability >= the unchanged frozen annual threshold. Only current and past windows are used. k=1 is the unchanged control.
alarm_delay: For each alarmed positive run, hours from its first positive-labelled window to its first alarm window inside the run. Reported, not gated.

acceptance.all_year_primary: per_year_primary holds in all six positive years for the same k
acceptance.zero_positive_2018: Report alarm episodes and FP only; recall and precision gains are undefined and not gated.
acceptance.probability_metrics: AP, Brier and log loss are unchanged by this rule and are not claimed as improvements.

inference: Per-year and pooled counts, plus paired full-HARP bootstrap (1000 draws, seed 24) for episode precision and FP difference versus control. Intervals are conditional on frozen predictions and thresholds; no multiple-comparison correction.
disclosure: k=3 and k=6 were chosen after seeing descriptive median all-negative episode lengths of 2 to 7 hours in the episode audit. No persistence result had been computed when this file was frozen.
scope: Adaptive development on already inspected years, not an independent test. A pass would only justify a separate prospective protocol, never an automatic change to alerts or models.
prohibitions: No other k values, cooldowns, merging or hysteresis after seeing results
No use of future windows in the rule
